title: The Chasm of Reverse Tolls

narrative.arrival: A sheer canyon cuts across the road. Three stone gates float above the mist, each glowing with an ancient toll balance. The bridge only appears if you know how many coins to set out with.
narrative.sealed: The third gate swings open with a deep chime. The stone bridge locks into place, the mist clears, and the path to the alchemist’s vault lies open.

inscription: A traveler crossed three magic toll gates on the road to the castle. At the first gate his pouch of Star-Coins doubled, then he paid 5 coins. At the second gate his coins doubled again, then he paid 3. At the third gate they doubled once more, then he paid 9. He walked into the castle with exactly 13 Star-Coins. How many did he start with?

parts.prompt: Find how many Star-Coins the traveler had in his pouch before crossing the first gate.

misconceptions.probe: At the third gate two things happened, one after the other. Walking backwards through that gate, which of the two do you meet first?
You gave all the tolls back at once. Does a toll paid at an early gate grow larger at the gates that come after it, or not?
Your start is tiny. Walk it forward through the first gate only. Does the pouch grow or shrink before the toll is paid?
We know the end of the road and we want the start. Which gate could we undo without guessing at all?

l0: Grubb says you're bluffing. I prefer a written account. In your own words, what number are we hunting, and what do we know for certain about the journey?
My gears work in order; these gates have an order too. Tell me the story of a single gate: what happened first, and what happened second?
Before we set off, let's mark what the inscription actually tells us. Which end of the road do we know for certain, the start or the finish?
l1: I once tried taking off my socks before my boots. A poor design. When we undo getting dressed, which thing has to come off first?
We could look at the road from the castle door. If you walked backwards from there, which gate would you reach first, and what would you have to undo?
Lemma keeps a card for journeys like this. Is there a card in the Deck that starts from the end of a story instead of its beginning?

l2.text: Each gate doubles the coins, then takes a toll. Backwards, we meet the payment first: return those coins, then undo the doubling. Which gate will you undo first, and what do you give back there?

l4.statement: A tiny road has one gate. Coins double, then he pays 3, and he leaves with 11. How many did he start with?
l4.l3: Give back the 3 coins he paid, then undo the doubling by splitting into equal halves. Count the start.

l3.text: Set the blueprint at the castle door with 13 coins. Give back the 9 paid at the third gate, then split the pouch in half to undo the doubling. What count belongs on that gate before we move on?

codex.oneLine: To undo a chain of steps, undo the last step first.
